question: If 70% of the cost price of an article is equal to 40% of its selling price, what is the profit percentage?
solution:
**Given :-**

70% of the cost price of an article is equal to 40% of its selling price.

**Concept Use :-**

Profit (p) = Selling price (s.p) - Cost price (c.p)

p% = (p/c.p) × 100

**Calculation :-**

Let c.p and s.p is x and y

⇒ p = s.p - c.p ..........(1)

⇒ 70% × c.p = 40% × s.p [ According to question ]

⇒ (70/100) × x =(40/100) × y

⇒ 7x = 4y 

⇒ y = 7x/4

Now,

Put the value of y in equation (1)

⇒ p = (7x/4) - x 

⇒ p = 3x/4

Now, 

⇒ p% = (3x/4/x) × 100

⇒ p% = **75%**

**Alternate Method :-**

⇒ 70% × c.p = 40% × s.p

⇒ s.p/c.p = 70%/40%

⇒ p% = (30/40) × 100

⇒ p% =** 75%**
